issues.problem: The brief asserts newly confirmed fast-track permitting and commissioning at month 20, while the September dossier retains unconfirmed access and permitting and month-36 commissioning. No dated update reconciles these accounts. Month 36 leaves only 12 months within the permitted project duration, making two full annual storage cycles impossible. T2 nevertheless requires month-20 commissioning as though its supporting status were settled.
issues.fix: Add a dated September update distinguishing confirmed commitments from proposed acceleration, reconcile the site schedule throughout the bundle, and provide a credible route to two complete cycles within 48 months. Make T2 assess the duration limit and feasible monitoring schedule without imposing month 20 as the uniquely acceptable solution.

issues.where: prior_project.md, system architecture and fossil-fuel displacement
issues.problem: The claimed gas displacement lacks a reconcilable system heat balance. Boiler heat falls from 22,500 to 3,600 MWh/year, a reduction of 18,900 MWh/year. The new heat pump supplies only 9,001 MWh/year, and storage loses 2,750 MWh/year. With unchanged demand and useful solar production, these figures leave 12,649 MWh/year unexplained. Solar thermal already existed in the baseline, but neither its baseline and intervention yields nor changes in demand are reported.
issues.fix: Provide annual baseline and intervention heat balances covering demand, useful solar production, direct heat delivery, storage flows, losses and curtailment. Identify any solar expansion or demand reduction explicitly, and revise the displacement and emissions results if those balances do not support them.
